notes: Fictional, equal-weight, complete cohort, not actual people and not a reconstruction or claim of national representativeness. Implements the requested 20-79-year analytical population as a transported distribution conditional on eligibility; no HbA1c, treatment or hypertension exclusion. Pregnancy and positive laboratory-weight/complete-case selection are not simulated as columns: their distributional effects are assumed absorbed into the explicitly assumed age/sex/BMI mixture. There is no evidence identifying selection into the laboratory-weighted complete cases, so age-decade masses [18,22,20,18,14,8]% and sex-age gradient are modeling assumptions, not survey estimates. ELSA-Brasil provides loose anchors only: female 54.4%, BMI mean 27.0 SD4.74, observed SBP121.3 SD17.3 and DBP76.3 SD10.8 in public servants aged35-74 at baseline2008-10 (Favaretto et al2025, Tables1-2 and Results, PMC12622929). We do not directly transplant its older age distribution. BMI age/sex pattern, skew, residual spreads, t tails, BP sex differences and age functions are assumed; their purpose is clinically plausible joint variability, not exact moment matching. The source's BP-category-specific summaries are not used because medication grouping makes them unsuitable for deriving a joint covariance. Any incidental comparisons with excluded surveys in the external paper's discussion are not used. Chen et al2015 PMC4537884 reports adjusted BMI slopes 6.7/3.6 mmHg SBP/DBP per5 BMI in53,578 rural Chinese adults not using antihypertensive treatment; it measured two readings and averaged them (occasionally last two after a third). These are transported as conditional slopes WITHOUT WC adjustment, not causal effects. Chen adjusted additional lifestyle covariates; using its slopes for the requested age/sex-only models assumes that their omission does not materially shift them. Transport from untreated lean rural Chinese adults to all-treatment Brazilian laboratory-eligible adults is unverified and may overstate associations; medication, diabetes and unobserved exposures are marginalized into observed BP intercepts/residuals rather than restricting the cohort or adding unrequested fields. Li et al2018 PMC6275465 motivates rising systolic age pattern and curved diastolic age pattern but was healthy Chinese adults, so no numeric slope is taken from it. No external joint residual covariance was identified: latent correlation0.65, within-reading correlation0.5 and measurement-error SD4/3 are explicit sensitivity assumptions, not published estimates. The requested residual correlation is not empirically identified by the univariate evidence; this generator supplies one scenario. Assumed aggregation is mean of two integer-valued final same-visit BP readings; output is in0.5 mmHg steps. There is a shared person/visit residual plus independent measurement errors across the two readings. The actual released final aggregation is unknown, so do not infer number of readings or within-person reliability from these data. BP represents baseline interview, not later laboratory-visit BP; no temporal alignment or BP change is modeled. Wide physiologic bounds and pulse-pressure>=15 are simulation safeguards, not assertions about unretrieved survey dictionary limits. BMI admissibility also uses assumed broad safeguards; weight and height are not separately generated. Paired rejection near bounds can modestly modify slopes/correlation. Analyze equal-weight OLS with intercept, age, female and(bmi-27)/5 for each BP, and Pearson correlation of the two fitted-model residual vectors. analyze(df) supplies these and a quadratic-age sensitivity; stochastic sample estimates differ from structural slopes. No exact coefficient enforcement or sample-level calibration, and no parameter-uncertainty resampling: varied seeds reflect individual sampling variability conditional on this one scientific scenario. For sensitivity studies alter covariance, treatment-transfer assumptions and aggregation using a separately versioned spec.

provenance.identifiability: Age-sex distribution of weighted eligible target, treatment-transfer effect and joint residual covariance unknown. All non-source-derived parameters labeled assumptions.
provenance.independence: No target study queried or used. An initial search containing excluded aliases in a NOT clause was blocked; subsequent searches used external cohorts only. Public source discussions can mention other surveys; such incidental national-survey figures were ignored.
